title: Leonida Ledger — GTA VI trophy data
disclaimer: Trophy names, official descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own, as reported by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this guide was written. Everything else here — the walkthrough text, the step lists and the timing advice — is written fresh for this guide from those official descriptions and general GTA play. The game only just launched, so where the official wording leaves a location or a trigger unstated, the guide says so plainly instead of guessing. There is no online trophy anywhere in the official 55.
cited_lists: PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: Nothing separate is asked of you here. This one simply appears the moment the other fifty-four are all done, so the way to earn it is to earn everything else, in the order the roadmap lays out: campaign first, then the side strands, then the activities, then the long sweeps, then the 100% checklist. Reported roadmaps put the whole journey at roughly two hundred hours.
steps: Finish the campaign and its named missions.
Clear the stranger strands, crime jobs and activities.
Sweep the collectibles, then close out the 100% checklist.
trophies.miss_risk: It cannot be missed on its own; it follows the last trophy you earn.
trophies.hint: The per-grade counts at the top of the page show what is still open — the last empty slot is your next job.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission, so this is the first trophy most players will see. Play the introduction at its own pace: get used to moving, driving and interacting as the prompts teach you, and follow the mission markers until the end card rolls. No preparation or side work is needed before it.
steps: Start the campaign and follow the opening prompts.
Learn the movement, driving and interaction basics as they appear.
See Gone Fishing through to its end card.
trophies.miss_risk: A story trophy — it comes from playing the campaign and cannot be missed.
trophies.hint: If you are brand new to the series, take the opening slowly; the controls it teaches carry through the whole game.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: A chapter in this game is a run of story missions, so closing Chapter 1 means finishing each mission in it in turn. Keep taking the next story marker as it shows up and work through the missions one by one; the trophy arrives with the chapter-complete screen. Side activities can wait — the chapter itself is only the story chain.
steps: Play the Chapter 1 missions in the order they appear.
Finish each mission; a failed attempt can be retried from its checkpoint.
Keep going until the chapter-complete screen shows.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; finishing the chapter is all it asks, so it cannot be missed.
trophies.hint: Before Chapter 1 ends, stop at the meditation spot listed under Positive Mental Attitude — that one may not wait.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 is the stretch where both leads become playable and far more of the map opens up, so expect fresh mission flavours and new faces alongside the main plot. The method stays the same as Chapter 1: follow the story markers, finish every mission the chapter hands you, and the trophy lands when the chapter closes.
steps: Follow the story markers through Chapter 2.
Try the newly opened parts of the map between missions if you like.
Finish the chapter's final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable as long as the chapter is finished.
trophies.hint: Both protagonists being playable means some missions suit one lead's skills better — swap when the game lets you.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 the story is properly inside Vice City, and the bigger robbery-style jobs the series is known for start to show up. Play the missions in order and see each one through to its end; the trophy is awarded at the chapter close, with no extra objective hiding behind it.
steps: Work through the Chapter 3 mission chain.
Stock up on armour and ammo between the bigger jobs.
Finish the chapter's last mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: Heist-style missions often end in a getaway drive — keep a fast car in mind before the job starts.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last full chapter before the finale, and its missions are the toughest story fights in the game. Go in prepared — armour, your best weapons, and whatever healing the game offers — and make use of cover and your partner in the heavier shootouts. Finish the chapter and the trophy is yours.
steps: Prepare between missions: armour, weapons and supplies.
Play the Chapter 4 missions in order, using cover in firefights.
Close the chapter with its final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: If a mission keeps beating you, drop the difficulty of your approach, not the mission — flank, use cover, and let your partner draw fire.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This is one of only two gold trophies, and it marks the end of the campaign. Before you start the finale, make a manual save in a separate slot: reported guides say the game has no mission replay, so that save is your only way back to the ending or to anything tied to it. Then play the final mission through to its conclusion.
steps: Make a manual save in a fresh slot before the finale.
Play the final mission to its end.
Keep that save — there is no mission replay to fall back on.
trophies.miss_risk: The trophy itself is unmissable, but without a save before the finale you cannot revisit the ending.
trophies.hint: Do any story-linked side business you care about before the finale, while the save is fresh.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is one of the named story missions, and named missions arrive in chapter order as the campaign advances. Keep playing the story until its marker appears on the map, then follow the objectives to the end of the mission. A failed attempt simply restarts from a checkpoint with your story progress intact.
steps: Advance the campaign until Breakfast Run appears.
Follow the mission objectives to the end.
Retry from the checkpoint if the mission fails.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: Named-mission trophies all work the same way — the campaign delivers them in order, so there is nothing to hunt for.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist: a setup phase, then the job itself, then almost certainly a getaway. Listen to the planning dialogue for what the game wants you to bring, do the job as directed, and drive clear once the take is in hand. The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in the campaign.
Follow the planning dialogue and bring the suggested gear.
Finish the job and the getaway drive.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: Heist missions reward a calm setup more than rushing in — read the plan before the shooting starts.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is another named mission in the campaign chain, so it turns up when the story reaches it. There is no side requirement and no special preparation — play the missions in order, take this one when its marker appears, and finish it. The trophy is awarded as the mission ends.
steps: Play the campaign until Child's Play appears.
Complete the mission objectives.
Collect the trophy at the mission-complete screen.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: If you lose track of where you are in the story, the mission list in the pause menu shows the next step.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a named story mission with a music and nightlife flavour. Expect a mix of driving, on-foot sections and one big set-piece moment, and follow the on-screen prompts through each beat. Play the campaign until the marker shows, finish the mission, and the trophy follows.
steps: Advance the story until Headliners appears.
Follow the prompts through the driving and on-foot sections.
Finish the set-piece and the mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: Set-piece missions sometimes swap your controls mid-mission — watch the prompts rather than mashing through them.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is set around Vice City International Airport, so expect an airport job: getting in, dealing with security or a target, and getting out. The mission's own objectives will tell you whether stealth or speed is wanted — follow them rather than forcing your usual style, and the trophy lands at the end.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in the campaign.
Read the objectives and match your approach to them.
Complete the mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: Airport missions punish wandering — stay on the mission path and the checkpoints keep you safe.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory sounds like a large operation, and the name is fair warning: expect heavy resistance and long firefights. Go in with full armour and your strongest weapons, move from cover to cover, and let your partner help when the game provides one. The trophy pops when the operation ends.
steps: Stock up on armour and ammo before starting.
Advance through the operation using cover.
Finish the mission for the trophy.
trophies.miss_risk: Story trophy; unmissable.
trophies.hint: In the big shootouts, clearing one side of the room before pushing forward beats sprinting into the middle.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Open the in-game completion checklist — Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion — and you will see the full list of tasks behind this gold trophy: story beats, side content and collectibles, roughly three dozen items by reported counts. Anything you already did counts, so work through the list last, category by category, using this guide's tracker to keep the categories straight. This is the second gold and the real gate to the Platinum.
steps: Open Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion to see the checklist.
Finish the story, side strands and activities first.
Clear the remaining checklist items one category at a time.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable: earlier progress counts, and nothing on the checklist is missable by reported guides.
trophies.hint: Do the checklist review only after the story — many of its boxes tick themselves while you play.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Stunts are the trick moves the game counts while you drive or ride: jumps, near misses, long airtime and the like. The total grows on its own if you drive hard, but to grind it, find a ramp or a hill, launch, land cleanly and repeat — a fast bike or car in open ground makes the loop quick. Keep an eye on the stunt total in the stats menu so you know how far along you are.
steps: Drive aggressively: jumps, airtime and near misses all count.
Find a ramp or hill and repeat clean launches.
Watch the stunt total in the stats menu.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; stunts can be done any time in free roam.
trophies.hint: Landing cleanly matters — a crash after a big jump can waste the stunt, so pick flat landing ground.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.official: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: There are nine activity types scattered around Leonida — racing, fishing, the shooting range, arcade games, bowling, drone racing, meditation, hunting and similar pastimes — and this trophy only asks you to sample each one once. You do not have to win any of them. Start one of each, tick it off in this guide as you go, and the trophy pops after the ninth type.
steps: Visit one activity of each type around Leonida.
Start it — a win is not required, one attempt is enough.
Tick each type off until all nine are tried.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; activities stay available in free roam.
trophies.hint: Several of these double as other trophies — bowling, fishing and the range each feed a second goal, so sample them early.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.official: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: There are forty-two Shooting Range challenges to gold, spread across the weapon classes the ranges offer — visit a range, usually at an ammunition store, and work through them one class at a time. Gold wants speed and accuracy together, so run each challenge slowly first to learn its target pattern, then push for the gold time. Use the weapon the challenge hands you, favour headshots where they score more, and retry at once: retries cost nothing.
steps: Find a shooting range at an ammunition store.
Learn each challenge's target pattern with a slow run.
Push for gold on every challenge, retrying freely.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; ranges stay open after the story.
trophies.hint: This is widely reported as the hardest skill trophy — leave it until your aim is warmed up, and do it in short sessions.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.official: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Fourteen Top Fun spots around the map host drone races, and you need a win at every one of them. Fly the drone through the checkpoints faster than the rival time or the opponent: learn each course's line before going for the win, cut corners through gates instead of around them, and stay smooth — a crash costs far more time than a cautious line saves. Note each location down as you win it.
steps: Find the Top Fun drone-race spots around the map.
Learn a course's line before racing it for the win.
Win at all 14 locations, ticking each off.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; race locations stay available.
trophies.hint: Fly the course once slowly to memorise the gates; the second run is usually the winning one.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty different races need winning — street races, off-road and water races are all spread across Leonida, and each distinct race counts once. Work through the race markers on the map instead of replaying one favourite. Choose a fast, good-handling car for road races, learn the braking points, and use the slipstream behind rivals on the straights.
steps: Find race markers across the map.
Win each distinct race once — replays of the same race do not count.
Keep going until twenty different wins are banked.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; races can be replayed and won any time.
trophies.hint: Water and off-road races need different vehicles from street races — match the vehicle to the surface before you start.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.official: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Fishing against Cal is a head-to-head: land the target fish, or the biggest total weight, before he does. Cast where the water ripples, reel steadily, and ease off when the fish fights so the line does not snap. Pick the bait the challenge hints at, and if you lose, challenge him again — the rematch uses the same setup.
steps: Find Cal's fishing challenge.
Cast at the ripples and reel steadily without snapping the line.
Beat his catch; retry the challenge if you lose.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the challenge can be retried.
trophies.hint: Patience beats speed here — a snapped line loses more time than a slow, steady reel.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Find an arcade cabinet — in an arcade, a bar or a similar venue — and play one game through to its end. No high score is needed, only a full completion, so pick the shortest or easiest cabinet you can find and see it through. That single completion is the whole trophy.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet in an arcade or bar.
Pick the shortest or easiest game on offer.
Play it through to its end.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; arcade machines stay playable.
trophies.hint: This also counts as one of the nine activity types for Master of None.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.official: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the strangers — the question-mark characters scattered around Leonida — and his trophy comes at the end of his whole mission strand. Take his missions whenever their markers appear and work through the chain in order; the trophy pops at the last mission's end. Stranger strands are easy to forget once the story moves on, so do them when you meet them.
steps: Find Andy's question-mark marker.
Play his missions in order as they appear.
Finish the strand's final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable, but stranger strands are easy to leave unfinished; do them when they appear.
trophies.hint: Clear stranger markers as you pass them — backtracking across the whole state later is the slow way.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.official: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand is another stranger chain, and the trophy waits at its final mission. Play his missions in order from the first marker onward. The name points at water, so expect at least one mission on or near it — keep a boat or a fast car handy when his missions start, and finish the last one for the trophy.
steps: Find Kenton's marker and start his strand.
Play the missions in order.
Complete the final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; finish the strand when it appears.
trophies.hint: Water missions are far easier if you arrive with a boat already nearby instead of hunting for one mid-mission.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.official: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand revolves around riding, so expect bike chases and deliveries on two wheels. Take his missions from the first marker, play the chain through in order, and the trophy unlocks at the last mission. Riding missions reward a steady hand more than top speed — crashing costs more than the seconds speeding saves.
steps: Find Billy's marker.
Ride his missions in order.
Finish the final mission of the strand.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; finish the strand when it appears.
trophies.hint: Keep a bike you like handy before starting his missions — the game may not hand you a good one.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.official: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight full stranger strands are needed, and a strand only counts when its final mission is done — starting one is not enough. Strangers are the question-mark characters in free roam, spread from Vice City out to the swamps and small towns, so explore the whole state and clear each strand as you find it. This silver sits above the five named stranger-final trophies as their umbrella.
steps: Explore the whole state for question-mark strangers.
Finish each strand's final mission — partial strands do not count.
Repeat until eight strands are complete.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable, but strands are spread across the whole map — check the far corners of Leonida.
trophies.hint: The five named stranger trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) are five of the eight — three more strands are still needed.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.official: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's chain is about supply runs: pickups, deliveries, and rivals who want the same goods. Take his missions when the marker appears, work through them in order, and see the strand through to its final mission. The trophy is the last mission's reward, not the first's.
steps: Find Randy's marker.
Run his supply missions in order.
Complete the final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; finish the strand when it appears.
trophies.hint: Delivery missions go smoother with a sturdy vehicle — rivals tend to ram, so avoid the fragile sports cars.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.official: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's strand is the last of the five named stranger chains: play his missions in order from the first marker to the last. If a mission in the chain fails, retry it — stranger strands pick up from the failed mission, so nothing you already finished is lost.
steps: Find Tyrone's marker.
Play his missions in order.
Finish the strand's final mission.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; finish the strand when it appears.
trophies.hint: A failed stranger mission is not a lost strand — retry from the checkpoint and carry on.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.official: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eighteen meditation spots are scattered across Leonida — quiet scenic places like beaches, overlooks and parks — and each one is revealed when you get close. Sit and complete the meditation at each. There are eighteen spots across ten locations, usable by both Jason and Lucia, and the count is tracked as you go.
steps: Visit meditation spots as you explore — they reveal when you get close.
Complete the meditation at each one.
Do the Chapter 1 spot before that chapter ends (see the warning).
trophies.miss_risk: THE ONLY POTENTIALLY MISSABLE TROPHY (PowerPyx). One spot — Lucia's balcony spot in Chapter 1 — is reported to disappear after that chapter, and the game has no mission replay. Meditate there before finishing Chapter 1, and keep a manual save at the start of every chapter as insurance.
trophies.hint: Make the Chapter 1 meditation the first thing you do when you spot it — it is the one spot you cannot come back for.
sources: PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap
Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.official: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret sends you after one specific animal — a rare or unusually large specimen, not ordinary wildlife. Follow the clues he gives you to its territory, approach downwind and quietly, and take the shot cleanly with a scoped rifle. Be patient: spooking the animal means a long stalk to find it again.
steps: Take Bret's hunt and follow his clues to the territory.
Approach downwind and quietly.
Take a clean shot with a scoped rifle.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the hunt can be retried.
trophies.hint: Move slowly once you are close — the animal's hearing will give you away before its eyes do.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Cards are hidden all over Leonida — in shops, houses, vehicles and out-of-the-way corners — and a set only counts when every card in it is found. Pick up every card you see while doing other things, and check the in-game collection screen to see which sets are nearly done, then hunt the missing cards deliberately. This is a silver and one of the longer collectible grinds.
steps: Pick up every card you pass while doing other things.
Check the collection screen for sets close to complete.
Hunt the missing cards until three sets are whole.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; cards stay collectible in free roam after the story.
trophies.hint: Cards hide in ordinary places as well as odd ones — check shops and houses, not just scenic spots.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK It is the in-game photo-style activity tied to landmarks and scenic spots: open it at a location the game offers and complete its prompt. The locations are spread across the whole state, so this pairs naturally with exploring every area for The Goodtime State. Watch the WAiNK count in the stats menu as it climbs toward one hundred.
steps: Explore Leonida and open WAiNK It at each offered location.
Complete the prompt at each spot.
Track the count in the stats menu toward 100.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; locations stay available in free roam.
trophies.hint: Do this on the same road trip as the area exploration and the card hunt — one drive, three trophies.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the small objectives the game tracks across driving, combat, exploration and activities — landing jumps, winning races, pulling off particular moves. Most of them complete on their own during a full playthrough; when you are short, open the challenges menu, find the ones closest to done, and mop up the easy, repeatable ones to reach fifty.
steps: Play normally — many challenges finish on their own.
Open the challenges menu to see which are close.
Mop up the easy repeatable ones until you reach 50.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; challenges can be finished any time.
trophies.hint: Short driving and combat challenges are the fastest mop-up — sort by nearest completion, not by what sounds fun.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.official: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, cause enough chaos to reach a four-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. Break line of sight once the fourth star appears: drive fast through alleys and off-road, switch vehicles, or hide until the flashing stars turn grey and the heat dies. Both characters must be together when the wanted level is lost, so do this during a mission or free-roam session where your partner is with you.
steps: Get your partner beside you in free roam or a mission.
Raise the wanted level to four stars.
Break line of sight and escape until the stars clear.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; wanted levels can be raised any time in free roam.
trophies.hint: A vehicle switch mid-escape drops the search faster than outrunning helicopters in the same car.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.official: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level alive the whole time — if the stars clear between robberies, the chain resets. Plan a route through three nearby shops, rob each quickly, and get back in the car fast. The trick is staying hot without getting caught: do not hide long enough for the heat to die, and do not get busted. A fast getaway car parked close to each shop makes the chain far easier.
steps: Pick three nearby shops and plan the route.
Rob each quickly with your partner, keeping the wanted level.
Do not let the stars clear or get busted mid-chain.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; retry the chain any time. Losing the wanted level mid-chain resets the count.
trophies.hint: Park the getaway car facing the exit before each robbery — the seconds you save leaving are the chain.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Every new vehicle model you drive for the first time counts — cars, bikes, boats, planes and more. Variety is the whole strategy: try everything you see parked or driving past, especially in different districts, since rare models spawn in particular areas. The discovered count sits in the stats menu.
steps: Drive every new vehicle model you see for the first time.
Try different districts — rare models spawn in specific areas.
Check the discovered count in the stats menu.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; vehicles keep spawning in free roam.
trophies.hint: A short hop in a parked car you have never driven counts — you do not need to keep it or drive it far.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.official: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming mode. Trigger it when a group of enemies is clustered together, then line up shots quickly while time is slowed. The best spot is a mission or shootout with several enemies in one room: wait until five are visible, switch Combat Focus on, and drop them one by one before the meter runs out.
steps: Find a shootout with several enemies clustered together.
Wait until five are visible, then trigger Combat Focus.
Drop all five before the meter runs out.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; retry in any firefight.
trophies.hint: Do not trigger it the moment you see one enemy — patience until the room is full is what makes the five.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.official: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: An unscheduled departure means stealing a plane and taking off without following the rules. Get onto the VCIA runways, take any aircraft, and get airborne. A wanted level will follow the moment you do it, so climb fast and fly away from the airport to complete the departure.
steps: Get onto the runways at Vice City International Airport.
Take any aircraft.
Take off and fly clear of the airport.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; VCIA stays accessible in free roam.
trophies.hint: Smaller planes get airborne quicker on a short runway — grab the first one you reach, not the biggest.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The joke in the description is the clue: it gets hot inside a Rhino tank. Steal a tank — from a military base or through a high wanted-level response — and drive it around while the army and police come for you. Survive the assault for a while and the trophy should pop. Keep moving, so sticky bombs and rockets have a harder time landing on you.
steps: Steal a Rhino tank from a military base or a high wanted level.
Drive it around while the response builds.
Keep moving and survive the assault.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; tanks can be found again in free roam.
trophies.hint: Movement is your armour here — a parked tank is a sitting target for rockets.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.official: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Go in quiet: enter when the store is calm, stay out of the cameras' line of sight, take the goods without smashing cases in front of the staff, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, leave and try again later — being detected voids the attempt, not the trophy.
steps: Enter a jewelry store when it is calm.
Avoid camera sightlines and take the goods quietly.
Leave before anyone raises the alarm.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; retry the robbery any time.
trophies.hint: Slow and quiet beats fast and loud here — the trophy is about never being seen at all.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Bank vault robberies are the big planned jobs of the criminal side content: crack the vault, grab the cash, then lose the wanted level that follows. Plan the getaway before you go in — a fast car parked nearby and an escape route that avoids the main roads — and repeat at five different banks. Each successful escape counts toward the five.
steps: Plan the getaway before entering: car parked nearby, route off the main roads.
Crack the vault and take the cash.
Escape the wanted level; repeat at five banks.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; bank vaults can be robbed again in free roam.
trophies.hint: The escape is the trophy, not the vault — a clean getaway matters more than a fast crack.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.official: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks drive set routes around the city. Spot one, block it or force it to stop, crack the rear doors, take the cash, then lose the wanted level. A sticky bomb on the rear doors is the classic GTA method; have your getaway car ready before you start, because the alarm goes up the moment the doors are hit.
steps: Spot an armored truck on its route and force it to stop.
Crack the rear doors and take the cash.
Escape in a getaway car parked nearby.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; armored trucks keep spawning on their routes.
trophies.hint: Learn one truck route first — knowing where it slows down tells you where to set the ambush.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Leonida is divided into fifty-two named areas — Vice City districts, beach towns, swamps, farmland and the Keys. Drive or fly through every one; the map fills in as you go, and the in-game stats show how many areas you have visited. Pair this with the WAiNK It locations and the card hunt so one road trip covers three trophies at once.
steps: Drive or fly through every named area of Leonida.
Watch the visited-areas count in the stats menu.
Sweep the remote corners last — swamps, farmland and the Keys.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the whole map stays open in free roam.
trophies.hint: A plane or helicopter turns the last few remote areas from a chore into a quick flyover.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.official: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Nine gangs run their own off-the-books operations around Leonida — drug labs, chop shops, smuggling spots — and you need to hit one operation belonging to each gang. The gangs are territorial, so each operation sits in a different part of the map; work through them district by district and keep count of which gangs you have already hit.
steps: Find each gang's illegal operation in its territory.
Rob the operation and escape.
Work district by district until all nine gangs are hit.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; gang operations stay available.
trophies.hint: Keep a written note of which gangs you have hit — nine similar robberies blur together fast.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.official: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: This is a quiet-moment trophy: no combat, no timer. Head to a bar or beachfront spot on Ocean Beach with an ocean view, order a cocktail, and take it in. The official description does not spell out the exact trigger spot, so try the beachfront bars along Ocean Drive and sit with the view until it pops — and treat any more precise claim as unverified until you see it yourself.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach and find a beachfront bar with an ocean view.
Order a cocktail and sit with the view.
If nothing pops, try another spot along Ocean Drive.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; Ocean Beach stays open. The exact trigger spot is not in the official description — verify in-game.
trophies.hint: Relaxing trophies like this one are best done between missions, when there is no wanted level chasing you.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.official: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out onto the street — the classic GTA showroom smash. Pick a showroom, get a fast car inside or aimed at it, and floor it through the front window. The trophy is about the spectacle, so commit to it and enjoy the alarms.
steps: Pick a vehicle showroom.
Get a fast car aimed at its front window.
Floor it through the glass and out onto the street.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; showrooms stay in the world.
trophies.hint: Speed matters more than the car — a long straight run-up at the window beats a fancy car with no room to accelerate.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.official: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Walk into the Kolt & Associates bowling alley, rent a lane, and play a full game — aim, pick your power, and roll. No particular score is needed; finishing the game is what counts. Bowling also counts toward the activity sampler for Master of None, so it is two birds with one lane.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Rent a lane and play a full game.
Finish the game — the score does not matter.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the alley stays open.
trophies.hint: A steady, repeatable throw beats trying to bowl a perfect game — you only need to finish.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description is deliberately vague — a partnership with mass appeal — so the honest guidance is to play the duo content: partner missions and activities together, and watch for a fame or public-reaction moment. The exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description, so verify the moment in-game rather than trusting a guess from any guide.
steps: Play partner missions and duo activities.
Watch for a fame or public-reaction moment.
Verify the exact trigger in-game — it is not in the official description.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable as far as the official description shows. The exact trigger is not spelled out — verify in-game.
trophies.hint: Vague trophies like this one usually pop during duo content — keep playing with your partner and it should come.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This trophy tracks a count of decisions you make across the game, reported to reach five hundred. Choices appear in missions, dialogue and side content: pick options, take sides, decide how a job goes. It builds up over a full playthrough, so just keep playing and choosing — it is a volume trophy, not a single moment.
steps: Keep making choices in missions, dialogue and side content.
Take sides and decide how jobs go when the game asks.
Let the count build over the full playthrough.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; choices keep appearing through the game. The count of 500 is reported by trophy trackers, not the official description.
trophies.hint: Do not rush choices to farm the count — a full playthrough with side content gets there on its own.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The name says it all: fail something, then get it right on the next try. Attempt a mission, challenge or activity, fail it, and then succeed on the immediate retry. If it does not pop, try a different repeatable activity — fail a race or a challenge once, then win it on the next attempt.
steps: Pick a repeatable race, challenge or activity.
Fail it once.
Succeed on the immediate next attempt.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; any repeatable activity works. The exact trigger is not spelled out in the official description — verify in-game.
trophies.hint: A short race is the easiest setup: losing one on purpose costs a minute, winning the retry costs another.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — one of Leonida's weird encounters. GTA games hide UFO sightings, cryptids and other odd events in remote places, usually at night or under particular conditions. Explore the swamps, the Keys and the far corners of the map, especially at night, and the trophy pops when you stumble into the strange event. The exact encounter is not in the official description, so treat this as an exploration trophy and verify the spot in-game.
steps: Explore remote Leonida — swamps, the Keys, far corners.
Go at night and under odd conditions.
Keep exploring until the strange event triggers.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the world stays explorable. The exact encounter is not spelled out — verify in-game.
trophies.hint: Night exploration of the swamps doubles as progress toward the area-exploration trophy, so combine the two.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.official: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: drive past a pedestrian and hit them with a melee swing from the vehicle. Get a slow-moving car or bike, equip a melee weapon, pull up alongside a pedestrian on a quiet street, and swing as you pass. It is a deliberately silly trophy — one clean hit is enough.
steps: Equip a melee weapon and get a slow car or bike.
Pull alongside a pedestrian on a quiet street.
Swing the melee weapon as you pass.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; try it any time in free roam.
trophies.hint: Slow is the key — at full speed you will miss the swing window entirely.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.official: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills are the dirty cash you pick up from robberies and heists; they cannot be spent directly, so you pass them to a contact who cleans them for a cut. Keep laundering after every big job and the total climbs. The count is cumulative across the whole game, so make laundering part of your routine after each score.
steps: Collect Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Pass them to a contact to launder.
Repeat after every big job until $250,000 is cleaned.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; laundering stays available all game.
trophies.hint: Launder little and often — letting dirty cash pile up means one big cut instead of many small ones, but the total is what counts.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Every dollar you spend in any shop counts — clothes, weapons, ammo, food, car mods. It builds up naturally over a full playthrough, especially once you start buying weapons and upgrading cars. If you are close near the end, buy expensive items — a high-end weapon or a full car upgrade — to close the gap. The total is cumulative and never resets.
steps: Spend normally in shops as you play.
Buy weapons and car upgrades — they move the total fastest.
Close any gap near the end with one expensive purchase.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; spending counts all game.
trophies.hint: Do not waste money early just for this trophy — the story's shopping will cover most of the hundred thousand.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Garages are buyable properties around Leonida that store your vehicles — eight of them in total. They cost money, so save up during the story and buy them as you can afford them; each purchase is also a safe place to stash rare cars you find. Check the property listings on the in-game map or phone to find the ones you have not bought yet.
steps: Save money during the story.
Check property listings on the map or phone.
Buy all eight garages.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; garages stay for sale in free roam.
trophies.hint: Buy a garage near where you usually work first — it doubles as storage for rare cars you stumble across.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI trophy list

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.official: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros is the in-game delivery and vehicle app on your phone: open it, add vehicles you own or find to the app, and repeat until ten are registered. Use a mix of cars and bikes you already own so you do not have to hunt for ten separate vehicles. The count is cumulative.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app on the in-game phone.
Register a vehicle you own or find.
Repeat with different vehicles until ten are registered.
trophies.miss_risk: Not missable; the app stays available all game.
trophies.hint: Your own garage is the fastest source — register the cars you already own before hunting for new ones.
